does: The handler of the Osiris call StartRespec(Target). Same shape as StartChangeAppearance: the character must be reserved for a user and carry eoc::CharacterCreationStatsComponent, the bytes at +0x250 and +0x288 of esv::character_creation::System must be clear; then the pair (character entity, unassigned user id) is appended to the system's request array at +0x438 (count at +0x444).

evidence.says: the registration of the Osiris game functions (code:unplaced::RegisterOsirisGameFunctions) pairs the text StartRespec with this address; the body checks ecs::HasComponent of eoc::CharacterCreationStatsComponent and writes into the array at +0x438 of the system taken by TypeIndex of esv::character_creation::System
a count-only probe shows no call of it during Osi.StartChangeAppearance

a count-only probe during Osi.StartRespec(host) shows one call, from bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x38248AA, and none of the handler of StartChangeAppearance; afterwards the server holds one entity with CCRespecDefinition and CCDefinitionCommon and a session entity with CCSessionCommon and CCRespec, the host reads CCState.HasDummy true, and the client opens the widget CharacterRespec on the same level
the macOS build's symbols hold this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows

questions.ask: call Osi.StartRespec(host) under a count-only probe on this address; the name esv::OsirisGameFunctions::StartRespec is by analogy with the Toolkit's text for StartChangeAppearance and is to be checked against EoCServer.dll
